newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has demanded that the decision of the two-day weekend be dropped.
Workers and employees of 13 sugar mills will observe agitation programmes on June 12 to protest the government's decision to privatise the units.
Angry villagers near capital Dhaka lynched six persons suspecting them to be cattle lifters in the early hours on Saturday.

Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), discussing with the government on funding a restructuring programme for Bangladesh Television, has expressed disatisfaction at the biased news coverage by the state-run media.
The government will realise over 20 billion taka in default bank loan within the current fiscal year ending June, Finance Minister S A M S Kibria said.
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Secretary General Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan on Saturday said the ruling Awami League has began the politics of "killing and repression".
Eight private jute mills were closed in last two years due to management inefficiency and inadequate working capital support from banks.
Bangladesh businessmen have urged New Delhi to do away with the requirement of 40 percent value addition to avail of the concessionary tariff benefit.
